_doc: The generic rules a row of tier plausible-procedural may name (field `rule`). A rule is a procedure, never a fact about a building: a row that uses it says in the product that the form is generic. The constants of the rules marked in_product are those of docs/battle-theatre/app/STRUCTURES-3D-NOTES.md section 6 (a generic value is not data about Gettysburg). A rule marked proposed is not drawn yet: it is the grammar the renderer still needs (a request note of the integration step asks for it, with the evidence rows that bear on it). A new rule is proposed in a group REPORT and added here by the integration step; a row never invents a rule id.

rules.statement: a storey is 3 m high; a house of no recorded storey count is drawn two storeys
rules.not_for: a building whose storey count a source gives

rules.statement: a gable roof of 30 degree pitch over the minimum bounding rectangle of the footprint, the ridge along the long side; flat for a borough mass
rules.not_for: a roof form or material a source gives

rules.statement: eave height of a house of two storeys: 6 m
eave height of a barn: 4.8 m; of a bank barn 5.2 m
eave height of an outbuilding: 3 m
eave height of an institutional building 7.5 m; of a church 7.5 m; of a college or seminary building 9 m; any other building 4.5 m
the 2023 outline of a surviving building stands for its 1863 footprint where no source dates the footprint; the 1863 form may be smaller (the card says so)
rules.not_for: a building with an altered or rebuilt outline unless a source says the 1863 outline is unchanged

rules.statement: a borough mass is the extent of the ink of the building symbols of the Warren plate (error 20 m): drawn two storeys high with a flat top, labelled schematic; it merges neighbouring buildings and may include buildings of 1863-69
a structure known only by a map-symbol point is a labelled pole; no building is invented at the point
post-and-rail fence 1.52 m high, panels 3.35 m, posts and four rails; the dimensions are generic and come from a non-Gettysburg source (about 11 ft rails, about 5 ft height)
rules.not_for: a fence whose type or height a source gives for Gettysburg

rules.statement: low field wall of loose stone 0.76 m high, 0.6 m thick (the Angle wall was originally about 2-3 ft); NEVER the 48-52 in. of the rebuilt park walls
turnpike 6.5 m, county road 5.5 m, township road 4.5 m, lane 3 m, railway bed 4 m, unfinished grade 5 m (the widths the base map draws, generic, not measured)
a road whose surface no source gives is dirt (most of the roads at the square were dirt); macadam only where a source names the road a macadamized turnpike
flat colours by material class (brick, stone, log, frame, generic), shingle roofs, charred when burned; no photograph is claimed

a building is drawn intact until a source dates a damage or use; no bullet hole, shell hole or fire is drawn that no source states (a count beyond a documented count is marked plausible-procedural by the damage rule of the renderer)
windows and doors are drawn in regular bays of the front wall, one door at the centre of a two- or three-bay front; no count is claimed
rules.not_for: a building whose openings a source or an 1863 photograph shows

rules.statement: one chimney at each gable end of a house of two or more rooms; none on an outbuilding without a stove or hearth
rules.not_for: a building whose chimneys a source or an 1863 photograph shows

rules.statement: no porch is drawn unless a source (or an 1863 photograph) names one: porches of 2023 are later additions until a text dates them
no sign or lettering is drawn unless a source names the business and the sign
